beats.say: The festive sale is six weeks away.
The order pipeline must survive an outage, keep payments correct, and stop bad files.
beats.label: The pipeline must

beats.say: Four ideas get you there. Let's go.
beats.label: Station 1.2 · Reliability and fidelity
beats.head: Four ideas for a pipeline you can trust

beats.say: First: which tool cleans the data?
Here is the trick. Pick the tool for the people who will run it.
beats.label: The trick
beats.head: Pick the tool for the people who run it

beats.say: A team that knows SQL, with data already in BigQuery? Dataform.
beats.label: SQL team
beats.head: Dataform
beats.text: SQL in BigQuery, with tests and Git

beats.say: A team that wants drag and drop, with no code? Cloud Data Fusion.
beats.label: No-code team
beats.head: Cloud Data Fusion

beats.say: Engineers with a fast stream and custom logic? Dataflow.
beats.label: Engineers with streams
beats.head: Dataflow

beats.say: And if you already have Spark jobs, keep them, on Dataproc.
beats.label: Existing Spark jobs
beats.head: Dataproc

beats.say: The trap: a no-code tool for a high volume, low latency stream.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: A no-code tool for a fast, high-volume stream

options: How long can we be down?
How much does the design cost?
How much data can we lose?
check.why: RPO is the data you can lose. RTO is the time you can be down.

beats.say: Second: what happens when something breaks?
Write down two numbers first. RPO: how much data you can lose.
beats.label: Number one
beats.head: RPO
beats.text: How much data can you lose?

beats.say: And RTO: how long you can be down.
beats.label: Number two
beats.head: RTO
beats.text: How long can you be down?

beats.say: Then buy the cheapest design that meets both. Not the fanciest.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: Cheapest design that meets both

beats.say: For Cloud Storage, a dual-region bucket with turbo replication gives an RPO of 15 minutes.
BigQuery has time travel. You can read a table as it was, up to 7 days ago.
Cloud SQL high availability keeps a standby in another zone. It takes over on its own.
beats.label: Cloud SQL HA
beats.head: A standby that takes over on its own

beats.say: But a read replica does not. You must promote it by hand.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: A read replica does not fail over by itself.

check.prompt: You must move money between two accounts. Which store is the wrong choice?
check.why: Bigtable is atomic for one row only. A transfer changes two rows.

beats.say: Third: keeping payments correct.
Moving money touches two rows. Both must change, or neither. That is a transaction.
beats.label: A transaction
beats.head: Both rows change, or neither

beats.say: Spanner does this across rows, tables, and even regions.
beats.label: Spanner
beats.head: Transactions across the globe

beats.say: Cloud SQL and AlloyDB do it inside one region.
beats.label: Cloud SQL · AlloyDB
beats.head: Transactions in one region

beats.say: Bigtable is atomic for one row only. So never use it to move money.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Bigtable is atomic for one row only.

beats.say: Stronger and wider guarantees cost more. Choose the weakest one that is enough.
beats.label: Rule of thumb
beats.head: Choose the weakest guarantee that is enough

beats.say: Fourth: stopping bad data.
Check the data in the place where it changes.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: Validate where the data changes

beats.say: Dataform has assertions. Dataplex has data quality scans.
beats.label: Where to check

beats.say: After a migration, the Data Validation Tool compares the source with the target.
beats.label: After a migration
beats.head: Data Validation Tool

beats.say: In Dataflow, send bad rows to a dead-letter table. Do not drop them, and do not crash.
beats.label: In a pipeline
beats.head: Bad rows go to a dead letter

beats.say: Quick recap.
Pick the tool for the team. Write down RPO and RTO first.
beats.label: Station 1.2 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Choose the weakest guarantee that works. And validate where the data changes.
beats.label: Station 1.2 · 2 of 2
